summary: This work develops a substrate-patterned fabrication technique for Josephson junctions that eliminates organic resists and intentional oxides near the junction by using three-dimensional step-and-undercut geometries etched into the substrate. The approach enables high-quality underdamped Nb/AlOx/Nb junctions across multiple geometries (step-edge insulated, cross-step insulated, Manhattan trench, and cross-trench) without lossy dielectric contamination, achieving $J_c R_n$ values of ~1.6 mV and $R_{sg}/R_n$ up to ~50.
motivation: High-melting-point superconductors like Nb and Ta can enable JJs operating above 300 mK and beyond 40 GHz, but conventional fabrication using organic resist lift-off fails at their higher deposition temperatures, while magnetron sputtering junctions suffer from nearby lossy dielectric layers that introduce excess noise.
method: Josephson junctions are fabricated by depositing trilayers (M1/TB1/M2) onto patterned Si substrates featuring step-and-undercut geometries that electrically isolate the junction electrodes; multiple implementations (SEI, cSEI, p-cSEI, MT, cT) are demonstrated with varying trench depths ($\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ in the range 100–450 nm) and material combinations, characterized via DC I-V measurements and microwave resonator quality factors.
result: SEI junctions with area $A = 100$ µm² exhibit $I_c = 110$ µA, $R_n = 12.7$ Ω, $V_g = 2.78$ mV, and pronounced hysteresis with low retrapping current; Nb CPW resonators show internal quality factors exceeding $3 \times 10^5$ at ~7 GHz; critical current density varies with oxidation parameters following a power law, with $J_c$ values ranging from 0.4 to 24.7 µA/µm² and effective undercut parameter $u$ from 0 to 1.4 µm across fabrication runs.
